author: Batcow
content:
TL;DR Cats just hit hard, wolves make your party  hit hard, bats make the enemy hit less hard.

I'm writing this as if the reader is a total noob so bare with me:

Faster pet attack speed is fucking amazing for hunters in PvP against casters because it causes spell pushback on anything with a cast time, but it's also useful in PvE too. You get more crits and therefore more Frenzy uptime. Bats from ZG and Broken Tooth are BiS for that since they have 1.0 attack speed.

Cats are generally better than bats for pure dps since cats have a x1.10 dmg modifier to base damage and bats have a x1.07. Cats also have access to both Bite and Claw, but also prowl which could come in handy in PvP. 

Bats have Bite and Screech. Screech does some direct damage but mostly it debuffs nearby enemies, dropping their attack power by 100 for 4 seconds at max rank. If you're going up against a really hard hitting physical damage boss like Patchwerk in Naxx then bats (or owls) might seriously be helpful in keeping tanks alive. Screech could also effectively be used against melee in PvP or for generating AoE threat while levelling/grinding. Good for survivability.

Wolves are another choice. They don't have any damage modifier like bats or cats do so they'll deal about 7-10% less dmg per swing and the fastest attack speed of any wolf is only 1.2 from Deathmaw (Rare) in Burning Steppes or Slavering Worgs from SFK. They [kinda] make up for this in that they have Furious Howl which at max rank adds about 51 extra damage to your next physical damage attack. This applies to your entire party within 15 yards which is great if your raiding party is mostly melee, but that 15 yards limit also means you gotta be a little closer to the boss or whatever you're fighting. If you're ever in a section where you can't attack with your pet then wolves are the best cuz you can have your wolf just stand by your side and buff you the entire time. Good multipurpose [but still not quite as much dps as bats or cats]

content: I have no idea what the level 44 meta is like, but at max level you should beat mages. Just lay a freezing trap before fight starts so they can't deadzone you as easily, unload as much damage as you can into them at range and slow them with concussive shot. If you get hit with frost nova use PvP trinket to escape or try and trap them if they get close enough. Don't let them sheep you, use FD or scatter to interupt it. They die extremely fast due to low hp so don't be afraid to run in and raptor strike them if it will finish them off.

author: Taintedlove
content:
Alright, I finally got DME lash farming down as Survival at lvl 54. Each run took me about 12 min with drinking and eating. I ended each pack with about 20-25 % health and almost OOM. 

 - Gear - I just went for a lot of mail gear with "of the Monkey" Suffix. Basically you want AP and stamina. I had 3.3k HP with talents.

 - Pet - For pets I used an Owl with Screech Rank 2 (I didn't train rank 3) because of the AoE threat, damage and melee AP reduction to enemies. I had it to only use Screech and nothing else.

 - Enchants and consumables- I used some Rugged Armour Kits on my gear just for that extra survivability. In hindsigt it was not needed, but it gave me more leeway to experiment. No healing potion was needed for any of the two runs of eight packs I did

 - Rotation - Set up an Explosive Trap at your target location and wait for the cooldown to refresh. Make sure your pet doesn't run for the mobs, since it can lead to mispulls from the elites. Use Explosive Trap on cooldown once every lasher is gathered, followed by Carve and fill in with Mongoose Bite and Raptor Strike. I used Aspect of the Monkey for that extra damage reduction from the 14 % dodge, giving me a total of about 25 % dodge.

 - Spec - Here is the spec I used. Nothing fance and could probably be used to DPS in a normal dungeon. https://talents.turtle-wow.org/hunter?points=FIDAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAANQCAVJQAbIQoBAA%3D

# **Turtle WoW - Hunter FAQ** (*by Dresche*) - **UPDATED FOR NIGHTMARES OF URSOL (1.18.1)**

I’m happy to share my comprehensive Hunter FAQ for Turtle WoW.
This document was created by me and has been proof-read multiple times by some of the best hunters on Turtle WoW (Dokka, Webecca, Beerwat, Nerfmepls). It reflects the best of the current knowledge about the class in Patch 1.18.

I am a hunter main since WoW Vanilla and my main reason for this FAQ is that the same questions keep appearing in the Hunter Discords over and over and I wanted to give new players an easy reference for the most frequently asked questions and limit misinformation that can be spread in this channel. Another motivation is to improve the reputation and skill of Hunters on Turtle WoW and beyond.

Hunters are one of the most beginner-friendly classes, but also one of the hardest to really master. They can provide immense fun and utility or wipe an entire raid. If this FAQ helps answer common questions, raise overall skill, and improve the standing of Hunter players on the server, it has already served its purpose.

The FAQ will be continuously updated as new findings come in. Where more testing is required (e.g., BM spec), entries are marked as TBD. Over time, additional questions or certain additions may be added. It’s a living document that will grow with the community.

author: Dresche

And in another Note. The question should not be if cat or Raptor is the Right pet. Both are great. Yes there are bleed immune mobs but Savage rend scaling is making up for that currently. A good hunter Can make both pets work. The difference is negligable in the grand scheme of things. 

The real question should be: How Can I maximise my pet uptime and thus Overall damage. And adjacent to that question, one should also ask, how one can excel at good pet managment. 

I still see hunters in random groups who forget to send their pet on mobs or send them far to late. My pet doesn’t do more damage because it’s a raptor or a cat. You Can make almost any pet work. Wind serpent, normal serpent, scorpid, cat, raptor, Wolf. Whatever. 

Pet uptime and good pet control are far more critical factors than what pet you play

author: Dresche
content:
Assuming you are lvl 60:
- spawn in with Mara staff
- run in the Princess direction but don’t go there. Take the left Bridge over the Pond where the crocodile Boss is. Run to the second to Last room before going down to the crocodile
- either use swiftness zanza or alternate between cheetah and monkey aspect (but don’t get hit when having cheetah aspect)
- start pulling the lasher packs with serpent Sting Rank 1 
- Go back the Same way you came from pulling all the packs near the Route 
- evade the Rocks by going around them (no need to pull them, as they will get aggroed by the lashers)
- arrive at the room with the hydras (the waterfall where you Ported in) 
- kite them around the rock formations in the hydra room
- when they are reasonably stacked start laying explosive traps and kill them all

Bonus advice:
- learn the Route by walking it a couple of times. When you succeed in going all the way without face pulling anything , then you are ready for the real pulls
- have a couple of swiftness potions when you are in a precarious Situation 
- pull by Running and doing 360 degree Jump shots. Learn that first if you are not comfortable doing it
- a frost trap here and there can buy you some seconds

Good luck and have fun. It’s Not the best farm in terms of gold, but it’s fun and trains your skills as hunter

author: Elmgren
content: you should be performing well by mostly just spamming the ability macro, always placing explosive trap in AoE situations and immolation on single-target. Your weapon does matter a lot. You're hardly gonna beat mages, rogues, warriors if you're outgeared by them. Also: do you always get Windfury? Always have all the offensive consumes on: mongoose, ground scorpok assay, elixir of giants, firewater/juju, sour mountain berry, elemental sharpening stone, str+agi scrolls. 8% hit is not needed when you have 305 weapon skill from the weapon skill quest. you only need 7%. with 310 weapon skill, you only need 6%. 315 weapon skill, hit cap=5%. author: Dresche
content:
Ah ok. As survival it depends a little bit on the mob situation that you find yourself in. 

In single target fights, dual wield can parse slightly higher due to double stats + higher swift aspects procs

In multi target fights, 2H can be better due to higher damage ceiling of the weapon itself which creates higher damage spikes for carve for example. 

Nevertheless in the end it depends on what weapons you can get your hands on quick. If you have a Naxx 2H and only dual wield from bwl, then I would definitely take the 2H over DW. Or the other way round
